case.description: Build a bounded review workflow for deciding whether a synthetic text classifier's proposed update deserves a further evaluation round. The task is to support that decision from supplied results and limited adjudication, without declaring deployment readiness.
case.valued_outcome: Produce a reproducible advance, reject or unresolved decision under the supplied acceptance rule, identify affected slices, and account for every adjudication used.
hard_constraints: Use only supplied records and labels; no outside examples.
Apply the stated acceptance rule without changing thresholds.
At most sixteen disputed labels may be adjudicated.
Report uncertainty when the adjudication limit prevents a supported decision.
resources: Eighty synthetic examples with baseline and candidate predictions, provisional labels and one of four slice identifiers.
A supplied rule: advance only if total correct predictions improve by at least four and no slice loses more than two.
A sealed adjudication table for twenty-four flagged labels, accessible one selected row at a time.
Spreadsheet or local script environment and seventy minutes of analyst time.
observations: Against provisional labels, the candidate gains six correct predictions overall.
One slice loses two and contains nine flagged labels.
Awkward observation: the slice with the largest apparent improvement also contains the most disagreements between the two supplied provisional annotators.

openings.claim: Make adjudication selection depend on remaining acceptance uncertainty. A paired-contribution interval ledger can support advance, reject or unresolved without treating provisional gains as confirmed.
openings.delta: Replace fixed record-ID inspection order with threshold-relevant ordering. For each unresolved flagged row, bound candidate-correct minus baseline-correct by [-1,1], or exactly zero when predictions agree. Sum intervals overall and by slice. Select reachable rows whose possible contribution changes can cross an acceptance boundary; prioritize the slice nearest failure, then total, then record ID. Recompute after each revealed label.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, identical bounds with fixed record-ID selection, prioritization should resolve more decisions within sixteen adjudications when reachable influential flags cluster near a binding threshold. The disagreement-heavy improvement slice may lose apparent certainty. No advantage is predicted when contributions are invariant or all influential rows are unavailable.
openings.probe: Run both orders on matched copies, each capped at sixteen adjudications and seventy minutes. Preselect the same four withheld rows; log unsuccessful access without charging allowance. Advance only when total lower bound is at least four and every slice lower bound at least minus two. Reject when total upper bound is below four or any slice upper bound below minus two; otherwise remain unresolved. Freeze reports before opening the full-label key. Compare key-conforming decisions, unresolved frequency, adjudications and elapsed time.
assumptions: Unflagged supplied labels are fixed review inputs; state this dependency explicitly. If their status is disputed, widen bounds or report unresolved.
Selection uses only supplied predictions, slices and flags; annotator disagreement is not an invented extra record field.

Defeat conditions include no ordering benefit, a key-disproved supported decision, or insufficient reachable influential labels. Sixteen rows may leave irreducible uncertainty; performance is unmeasured.

openings.claim: Replace a single provisional confusion table with an adjudication ledger carrying conservative bounds on candidate-minus-baseline correctness, overall and by slice. Advance only when every remaining label assignment passes; reject only when none passes; otherwise report unresolved.
openings.delta: Change the decision dependency from provisional point counts to unresolved-label bounds, and selection from fixed record order to threshold-sensitive differing-prediction rows. Identical predictions contribute zero regardless of label; an unresolved differing-prediction row conservatively contributes between minus one and plus one. Keep nonflagged supplied labels fixed. Prioritize the slice at minus two and disagreements in the apparent gain slice by which adjudication could change the possible decisions; break ties by record identifier.

It should not produce a supported decision inconsistent with the full-label key. A concentration of unresolved influential rows in withheld records may defeat the selection advantage.

Aggregate total and slice bounds. Select a flagged row whose possible resolutions most change certification of an acceptance clause, breaking ties by record identifier.

The differing observation is a frozen supported verdict versus unresolved, checked against the full-label key. This advantage is hypothetical.

Maintain a ledger of identifier, selection reason, access outcome, adjudication count and elapsed time. Reject only when the total upper bound is below four or some slice upper bound is below minus two.
